requirement: Test the current IR expression vocabulary (lib/contract-model/ir/types.ts) against 10 synthetic scenarios A-J. If the IR CANNOT represent one or more generically: STOP implementation, produce an IR architecture proposal first. Do not work around an inadequate IR in prompts.
irExpressionVocabularyConfirmed: MONEY / NUMBER / PERCENT / RATIO / BOOLEAN_LITERAL / DATE_LITERAL (literals)
METRIC_REFERENCE / DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE / RULE_REFERENCE / LEDGER_USAGE_REFERENCE / TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE / ENTITY_SCOPE_REFERENCE (references)
ADD / SUM / MULTIPLY / SUBTRACT / DIVIDE (arithmetic, n-ary and binary)
SCHEDULE (cases + defaultValue - purpose-built for tiered/pricing-grid structures)

representabilityTests.scenario: Additive metrics (N-way sum of named components)
representabilityTests.mechanism: ADD/SUM over METRIC_REFERENCE/DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE operands, any arity.
representabilityTests.confidence: HIGH - directly exercised by the real B4 holdout claim (2 real ADD/MIN/SUBTRACT rules produced).

representabilityTests.scenario: Capped addbacks (an addback limited to the lesser of a stated dollar figure and a percentage of a base metric)
representabilityTests.mechanism: MIN(statedDollarFigure, MULTIPLY(PERCENT, METRIC_REFERENCE)) - MULTIPLY explicitly supports PERCENT as a scaling factor over a MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO base (type-check.ts:56-71), and MIN takes any MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO operands of matching type.
representabilityTests.confidence: HIGH - type rules directly support this composition; B4's real MIN(...) rule is a structural precedent.

representabilityTests.scenario: Aggregate caps (a cap applied across the SUM of several distinct addback categories, not any one category individually)
representabilityTests.mechanism: MIN(ADD(category1, category2, ...), capValue) - the cap wraps the aggregate ADD, not each addend; no new node kind needed.

representabilityTests.scenario: Acquired-EBITDA / run-rate-synergy caps (a sub-cap limited to a percentage of a DIFFERENT metric than the top-level definition being computed, e.g. 15% of Acquired EBITDA nested inside a Consolidated EBITDA addback)
representabilityTests.mechanism: MIN(synergyAmount, MULTIPLY(PERCENT, METRIC_REFERENCE('Acquired EBITDA'))) nested as one operand of the outer ADD - METRIC_REFERENCE can name ANY defined metric, not only the one currently being computed, so cross-metric caps compose without a new primitive.

representabilityTests.scenario: Ratio definitions (a metric expressed as one quantity divided by another, e.g. Secured Net Leverage Ratio = Secured Debt / EBITDA)
representabilityTests.mechanism: DIVIDE(numerator, denominator), both operands MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO-typed; DIVIDE's own type-check (type-check.ts:79-86) explicitly returns the node's declared RATIO type for MONEY/MONEY division.

representabilityTests.scenario: Pricing grids / tiered structures keyed to a ratio threshold (a lookup table of basis-point margins by leverage-ratio tier)
representabilityTests.mechanism: SCHEDULE(cases: [{from, to, description, value}], defaultValue) - purpose-built exactly for this shape; each case's `value` is itself a full IRExpression (so a case value can be MONEY/PERCENT/RATIO/etc.).
representabilityTests.note: The real B2 holdout claim (Applicable Rate, a pricing grid) was compiled by the model as nested IF rather than SCHEDULE and failed via the SAME poison-propagation defect as ADD/SUBTRACT (see 01, IF's type-check.ts:116-124 rule). This does not mean SCHEDULE is inadequate - it means the model did not choose the purpose-built node for this instance. SCHEDULE's own representability is unaffected; whether to nudge model behavior toward SCHEDULE for grid-shaped definitions is a PROMPT_INSTRUCTION-layer decision, not an IR gap (see 04).

representabilityTests.scenario: Greater-of / lesser-of clauses (a value defined as the greater or lesser of two or more alternatives)
Nested conditions and provisos (a definition whose applicability or amount depends on a triggering condition, e.g. 'provided that if X has occurred, Y shall not exceed Z')
representabilityTests.mechanism: IF(condition, then, else) for value-level branching; EVENT_ACTIVE(eventDescription, triggerCondition, activeDuration) for provisos gated on a triggering event/condition being currently active; AND/OR/NOT/COMPARE compose arbitrarily complex boolean conditions from these.

representabilityTests.scenario: Maintenance-liquidity formulas (a liquidity metric computed as a sum/difference of cash-like balances against available facility capacity, evaluated against one or more dollar thresholds)
representabilityTests.mechanism: ADD/SUBTRACT over METRIC_REFERENCE/LEDGER_USAGE_REFERENCE operands, compared via COMPARE against MONEY literals or further METRIC_REFERENCE thresholds.
representabilityTests.confidence: HIGH - directly exercised by the real B4 holdout claim's Maintenance Liquidity definition (ADD, sufficiency COMPLETE).

representabilityTests.scenario: Cash-sweep-cure mechanics (a deficiency amount computed from a shortfall against a threshold, with a defined cure window/mechanism)
representabilityTests.mechanism: SUBTRACT(threshold, actualBalance) for the deficiency amount; EVENT_ACTIVE/DURING_PERIOD for the cure-window temporal scoping; AS_OF for point-in-time thresholds.
representabilityTests.confidence: HIGH - directly exercised by the real B4 holdout claim's Deficiency Amount definition (SUBTRACT, sufficiency COMPLETE) - this is not hypothetical, it is observed production output.

gateOutcome: IR is NOT representability-inadequate for the mission's own A-J synthetic test set. Per the mission's own Section 13 instruction ('If current IR CANNOT represent one or more of these generically: STOP implementation'), this condition is NOT triggered - proceeding to implementation is permitted, not blocked.

residualFindingOutOfScope.description: The real holdout (not the A-J synthetic set) surfaced ONE genuine, narrow representability gap not covered by A-J: a categorical inclusion/exclusion FILTER over a SET of legal instruments (A4/Consolidated First Lien Secured Debt - 'the aggregate outstanding principal amount of Indebtedness meeting inclusion criteria X/Y/Z, minus exclusion criteria D/E/F, with a nested carve-back re-inclusion for G'). This is structurally a scope/eligibility test over a collection of items, not a formula over already-known scalar metrics - none of ADD/SUM/SUBTRACT/MULTIPLY/DIVIDE/MAX/MIN/COMPARE/IF/SCHEDULE model 'aggregate of items satisfying a predicate.'
residualFindingOutOfScope.disposition: Disclosed honestly, NOT remediated in this mission. Rationale: (1) it is outside the mission's own A-J representability test scope, so the mission's own STOP-and-propose-first gate is not triggered by it; (2) adding a new SET_FILTER/eligibility-aggregate expression kind is a materially larger, riskier IR schema change than this mission's bounded remediation charter contemplates, and the mission explicitly instructs against schema migration 'unless truly unavoidable'; (3) it affects exactly 1 of 10 real holdout claims (A4's Consolidated First Lien Secured Debt sub-claim), and the mission's own semantic pass gate tolerates up to 1 safely-surfaced miss among A1-A6 - so this residual gap does not, by itself, block the mission's own numeric gates. It is recorded here as a follow-up architecture item for a future, separately-scoped session (a candidate future IR extension: a bounded SET/AGGREGATE-WITH-PREDICATE node), not swept under the rug.

conclusion: PROCEED TO IMPLEMENTATION. No IR architecture rewrite is required. The dominant real-holdout defect (buildComposite/inferType poison-propagation discard, see 03/04) is a normalization-layer bug, not an IR-vocabulary gap - it manifests as composites failing to preserve already-correctly-typed sibling structure, not as an inability to express the underlying financial concepts.
